title: Borrowing Smart
blurb: Loans, APR and how to avoid expensive mistakes.
cards: Common options: credit cards, personal loans, buy-now-pay-later and overdrafts. They all cost money, but the cost can be very different.
Which statement about borrowing is true?
It is free if you pay later
You repay what you borrowed plus the cost of borrowing
The cost is interest and sometimes fees.
APR is the yearly cost of a loan including interest and some fees. Use it to compare offers: a lower APR means a cheaper loan.
Loan A has 8% APR and Loan B has 22% APR, same amount. Which is cheaper?
Lower APR means you pay less to borrow.
Buy-now-pay-later is always free because there is no interest.
Late fees and overspending can make it expensive. Treat it like any other debt.
Before borrowing ask: what is the monthly payment, how many months, and can I afford it if my income dips? If you cannot answer, wait.
Which is the best reason to borrow?
To pay for something that helps you earn more, like a needed tool or course
To pay a small bill you could cover
Borrowing makes most sense when it builds earning power and you can afford the repayments.
example: Two loans offer the same amount but different total repayments. Compare the full amount repaid and all fees, not only which monthly payment looks smaller.
